projects.title: DLD Security Digital Logic Circuit
projects.tagline: Designed and physically implemented a NAND-based digital encryption and decryption circuit.
projects.summary: A hardware-based digital logic project involving the design, simplification, and physical implementation of an encryption/decryption circuit using NAND gates, DIP switches, a BCD decoder, and a seven-segment display.
description: ecurity Digital Logic Circuit was a multi-stage Digital Logic Design project focused on designing and physically implementing a simple encryption/decryption system using fundamental digital logic concepts.

The project began by defining the required encryption and decryption mappings through truth tables. Karnaugh maps were then used to simplify the Boolean expressions for each output bit before converting the resulting logic into NAND-gate-only implementations.

The design was subsequently translated into physical hardware using DIP switches, a BCD decoder, resistors, and a seven-segment display. The final circuit connected the NAND-based encryption/decryption logic to the display system, allowing the resulting encoded values to be verified directly through hardware.
The project provided hands-on experience in moving from Boolean logic and mathematical simplification → logic-gate implementation → physical digital hardware.
stack: Digital Logic Design · NAND Gates · Karnaugh Maps · Boolean Algebra · Breadboard · DIP Switches · BCD Decoder · 7-Segment Display

projects.title: Audio Processing & Noise Cancellation
projects.tagline: Generated piano melodies in Python and developed frequency-domain noise cancellation using FFT analysis.
projects.summary: A Python-based audio signal processing project that generates piano melodies from sinusoidal signals, introduces simulated noise, analyzes signals in the frequency domain using FFT, and removes unwanted frequencies through frequency-domain filtering.
description: Audio Processing & Noise Cancellation was a Python-based Signal and System Theory project focused on generating, analyzing, and processing audio signals.

The project began by generating individual piano notes as sinusoidal signals using their corresponding frequencies from the 3rd and 4th piano octaves. Multiple note pairs were then combined to create a complete musical signal that could be visualized and played as audio.

To simulate real-world interference, sinusoidal noise components at randomly selected frequencies were added to the generated song. The noisy signal was then transformed into the frequency domain using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), allowing the dominant frequency components associated with the noise to be identified.

After detecting the unwanted frequencies, the corresponding frequency components were filtered out before transforming the signal back into the time domain. The resulting signal was then compared with the original and played back to evaluate the effectiveness of the noise cancellation process.
The project provided practical experience with digital signal generation, Fourier analysis, frequency-domain processing, visualization, and audio manipulation using Python.
stack: Python · NumPy · Matplotlib · SciPy · SoundDevice · FFT · Digital Signal Processing

projects.title: Band-Pass / Band-Stop Filter Design
projects.tagline: Designed, simulated, and physically implemented an analog frequency-selective filter.
projects.summary: Designed and implemented an analog filter by selecting component values, validating its frequency response through PSpice simulation, and testing the physical circuit using a breadboard and oscilloscope.
description: Analog Filter Design & Hardware Implementation was an Electric Circuits II project focused on the design and physical implementation of a frequency-selective analog filter.

The project involved selecting appropriate resistor and capacitor values to achieve a desired frequency response while maintaining practical component values for hardware implementation. The designed circuit was first simulated in PSpice, where its frequency response was analyzed using AC sweep simulations and its behavior was evaluated at frequencies below, at, and above the target frequency.

After validating the simulation results, the circuit was physically constructed on a breadboard using an operational amplifier, resistors, capacitors, and jumper connections. The hardware implementation was then tested using a function generator and oscilloscope to measure the input and output signals and verify the filter's frequency-selective behavior.
The project provided practical experience in analog circuit design, frequency-response analysis, circuit simulation, hardware prototyping, and experimental validation.
stack: PSpice · LM741/LM324 · Breadboard · Oscilloscope · Function Generator · Resistors · Capacitors

projects.summary: Developed a complete Java game engine for a customized single-player Jackaroo experience against three CPU players, implementing card mechanics, marble movement, collisions, and turn-based gameplay.

Implemented the core game architecture including the board, players, CPU opponents, marbles, cards, deck, safe zones, traps, firepit, turn management, rounds, and win conditions.

projects.title: Basic Computer & CPU Control Unit
projects.tagline: Designed and simulated a basic computer architecture and its control unit using Logisim.
projects.summary: Built a simplified 16-bit computer from the ground up, implementing a shared-bus architecture, registers, RAM, ALU operations, and a custom control unit to execute assembly instructions.
description: Designed and implemented a simplified 16-bit basic computer architecture using Logisim as part of the Computer Organization and Systems Programming course at the German University in Cairo.

Built the core hardware components including a 128×16 RAM, common system bus, Address Register (AR), Data Register (DR), Accumulator (AC), Temporary Register (TR), Program Counter (PC), and Instruction Register (IR).
Designed the ALU to support arithmetic and logical operations including addition, multiplication, AND, data transfer, and complementation, with dedicated control signals for each operation.
Developed the CPU control unit using decoders, a sequence counter, and logic gates to generate the required control signals for each instruction and clock cycle.

Implemented the instruction cycle and control logic for LDA, ADD, AND, STA, ISZ, BUN, and a custom MUL instruction, allowing the simulated computer to execute an assembly program involving arithmetic operations, memory access, branching, and loops.
Tested the architecture with different input values and verified the resulting memory and register states across individual micro-operation and timing cycles.

projects.title: Prolog and haskel projects
projects.tagline: Exploring logic and functional programming through scheduling and graph algorithms
projects.summary:
Implemented two programming-language projects using Prolog and Haskell, covering constraint-based university scheduling and shortest-path railway network analysis with Dijkstra’s algorithm.

Full description
description: Project 1 — Class Scheduling (Prolog)

Developed a Prolog-based university course scheduling system that generates valid schedules for students while satisfying constraints such as avoiding course clashes and limiting the number of study days per week. Implemented predicates for generating individual and university-wide schedules, validating clashes, calculating study days, and identifying common assembly hours.
Project 2 — Railway Network (Haskell)

Developed a railway network represented as a weighted directed adjacency matrix and implemented Dijkstra’s shortest-path algorithm to calculate the minimum traversal cost between stations. Built a recursive priority queue data structure and implemented network generation, edge modification, source initialization, and shortest-path computation.
Key concepts demonstrated: logic programming, functional programming, recursion, constraint satisfaction, graph representation, priority queues, and shortest-path algorithms.

projects.title: Smart Self-Driving Car
projects.tagline: A digital control system that detects lane deviation, obstacles, and gas leakage
projects.summary: Designed and implemented a smart self-driving car system that follows a designated lane, detects obstacles, and responds to gas leakage with automatic stopping, visual alerts, and an audible warning.
description: Smart Car — Digital System Design Project

Designed and implemented a digital smart-car system capable of autonomously responding to multiple environmental conditions. The car uses sensors to follow a designated lane and continuously monitors its surroundings for potential hazards.

A lane-detection sensor identifies when the car drifts outside its designated lane and triggers an “ALERT” warning on a 7-segment display. An obstacle-detection sensor monitors the path ahead and automatically stops the car when an obstacle is detected.
The system also incorporates gas-leakage detection. When gas leakage is detected, the car immediately stops, activates a red warning LED, and produces an audible warning signal.
The project integrated sensors, digital logic, control signals, visual indicators, audio output, and a moving mechanism into a single autonomous safety system.

projects.title: Operating System Simulator
projects.tagline: Java-based operating system simulator implementing process scheduling, memory management, synchronization, and system calls.
projects.summary: Developed a simulated operating system in Java that interprets and executes programs while managing processes, memory, system calls, mutex synchronization, scheduling, and disk swapping. Implemented HRRN and Round Robin scheduling alongside process state management and a real-time Java GUI for visualizing system execution.
description:
Built a program interpreter capable of parsing and executing custom OS instructions.
Implemented process management using Process Control Blocks (PCBs) containing process state, program counter, process ID, and memory boundaries.
Designed a 40-word simulated memory with process-specific memory allocation and protection.
Implemented disk swapping when available memory was insufficient, allowing processes to be unloaded and restored dynamically.
Developed system calls for file I/O, user input/output, and memory read/write operations.
Implemented mutex synchronization for shared file access, user input, and screen output using semWait and semSignal.
Implemented HRRN non-preemptive scheduling and Round Robin preemptive scheduling with configurable time slices.
Implemented Multi-Level Feedback Queue (MLFQ) scheduling as an additional feature.
Managed Ready and Blocked queues and process state transitions.
Built a Java GUI to visualize queues, memory, process execution, scheduling events, and disk swapping in real time.
stack: Java · Operating Systems · Process Scheduling · Memory Management · Concurrency · Synchronization · System Calls · JavaFX / GUI

Simulated clock-cycle execution and tracked pipeline stages, register updates, and memory changes throughout program execution.
description:
Designed a complete processor simulation with registers, program counter, instruction memory, and data memory.
Implemented a custom Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) with binary instruction encoding and decoding.
Built a pipelined datapath with Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory, and Write Back stages.
Simulated multiple instructions executing concurrently across pipeline stages.
Implemented branch and jump instructions with pipeline flushing and control-hazard handling.
Implemented data hazard handling using appropriate stalling/forwarding techniques.
Implemented arithmetic and logical operations with carry, overflow, negative, sign, and zero flags.
Simulated clock-cycle-level processor execution, tracking stage inputs, outputs, register updates, and memory changes.
Implemented signed two's-complement arithmetic and appropriate 8/16/32-bit data representations.
Generated detailed execution traces showing pipeline state and final processor/memory contents.

The platform aims to provide a centralized space where students can showcase academic projects, build portfolios, collaborate with teammates, and make their work discoverable to peers, instructors, and potential employers.

Milestone 1 focused on Requirements Engineering, where the system requirements were analyzed and documented as 100 functional user stories covering students, instructors, employers, and administrators, alongside 10 non-functional requirements. The project emphasized usability, responsiveness, consistency, navigation, learnability, and professional UI/UX design while following software engineering and requirements engineering principles.
MS1: Requirements Engineering — 100 functional user stories + 10 NFRs

projects.title: Data Bases II — DBMS Implementation
projects.tagline: A Java-based database management system implementing storage, querying, bitmap indexing, tracing, and data recovery.
projects.summary: Implemented core DBMS functionality from scratch in Java, including table creation, page-based storage, record insertion and selection, bitmap indexing, operation tracing, and page-level data recovery.
description: Developed a database management system in Java as part of the German University in Cairo's Data Bases II course, focusing on understanding and implementing core DBMS components and their behavior.

The first milestone implemented table creation, record insertion, page-based storage, multiple forms of record selection, direct record access through page and record pointers, and operation tracing. The system serializes table metadata and pages to disk and maintains detailed execution traces for database operations.

The second milestone extended the DBMS with bitmap indexing and indexed selection. Bitmap indexes can be created for specific columns, automatically updated when new records are inserted, and used to optimize conditional queries through combinations of indexed and non-indexed conditions.

The project also implements page-level data validation and recovery. The system can detect missing pages, identify lost records, and restore the missing pages and records to their original locations while maintaining the database trace.
The project provided practical experience with database storage architecture, serialization, page management, indexing, query processing, data recovery, and performance-oriented database operations.

projects.title: Microsoft × Sprints — Heart Disease Prediction Project
projects.tagline: End-to-end machine learning for heart disease risk prediction
projects.summary: Built an end-to-end machine learning pipeline for heart disease prediction, combining data preprocessing, multiple classification models, and probabilistic risk analysis.
description:
Full description
Developed a complete machine learning pipeline for predicting heart disease risk, covering data preprocessing, feature selection, model training, evaluation, and visualization.

Implemented and compared Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Means models using Python and Scikit-learn to explore different approaches to cardiovascular risk prediction.
Extended the project with probabilistic risk prediction using PyMC and NUTS sampling, providing a Bayesian approach to estimating individual risk.

Completed as part of the Microsoft × Sprints 2025 program.

projects.title: Mailwise AI
projects.tagline: An AI-powered assistant for a smarter inbox.
projects.summary: A full-stack AI email assistant that connects to Gmail to classify, summarize, prioritize, and generate context-aware reply suggestions.
description: Mailwise AI is a full-stack AI email assistant designed to make managing a busy inbox faster and more intelligent. It connects to Gmail through the Gmail API and Google OAuth 2.0, retrieves email content, and uses AI to help users understand, organize, and respond to their messages.

The system can classify emails, generate concise summaries, identify important messages, and create context-aware reply suggestions. It separates the frontend, backend, authentication, Gmail integration, AI services, database, and business logic into modular components.

The backend is built with FastAPI, Pydantic, and SQLAlchemy, while the interactive frontend is built with Streamlit. The AI layer uses Gemini and follows a configurable provider architecture, allowing different AI providers to be integrated without changing the core application.
The project also includes automated backend testing with Pytest and uses environment-based configuration to keep API keys and authentication credentials separate from the application code.
